title: A completion queue
description:
Model I/O completion ports: start operations, and let worker loops handle them as they finish.

```
start read #1 (takes 30 ms), read #2 (10 ms), write #3 (20 ms)
t=10 completed #2 read 512 bytes -> handler started a write #4 (5 ms)
t=15 completed #4 write
t=20 completed #3 write
t=30 completed #1 read 4096 bytes
```
hints: The "clock" jumps to each completion's finish time; a new operation finishes at `now + duration` (lesson 2.05).
Real IOCP gives you an `OVERLAPPED*` back; here the `Op` itself plays that part, so keep the id to find your own state.
requirements: Operations have an id, a kind, a finish time and a result; a priority queue ordered by finish time stands in for the port.
`getQueuedCompletion()` returns the next finished operation; a handler may start new operations.
Track how many operations are in flight and finish when it reaches 0.
stretch: Run two "worker threads" that take turns taking completions, and show that order of handling is not the order of starting.
